rationale_bullets: Hoover (76.8/480; 3,472 yds, 29-13, school single-season record holder) left for Indiana - the one meaningful defection from an elite-retention roster.

Jaden Craig arrives as Harvard's all-time passing leader (6,074/52 career; 52-12 TD-INT; 2,889 at 61.5% with 25-7 in '25, 1st-team Ivy) - 'top 10 QB NFL prospect' (PS), unquestioned starter (P6), with mobility at 6'3 230.
The FCS guard bites hardest here: zero FBS snaps, P6-flagged accuracy, and a simultaneous new pro-style OC install (Sammis).
46 = fringe-below-average: ISU's Raynor earned 48 with three years of FBS tape; Craig's buzz is higher, his level is lower.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Ivy/FCS production graded with the hardest level discount in the set; NFL-prospect framing keeps it at 46 rather than lower

rationale_bullets: Payne (77.6; 623 at 5.7) returns off the late surge - 174 vs Cincinnati, 103 vs Houston, the four-tackle-breaking OT winner vs USC - with P6 projecting 1,000 as Sammis tilts run.
Battle (72.8; 349 at 5.5 in '24) and Denman (69.8; 178 as a true FR) give proven depth; Barnes (77.3, injured mid-year) expired.
'25 RUN was 51st pctile on a committee and nobody has carried a lead-back load (Payne 109 carries); the room is good tape without proven volume. 52 = average-plus.
The 90th-pctile RECV engine departs: McAlister (76.1; 1,190/10, 3rd-team AA, Biletnikoff semifinalist), Manjack (69.9; 579), TE Rogers (72.4; 319).

Dwyer (71.1; 730/7, 3rd-team B12) steps up as the #1; TE Pimpton (Top100 pedigree; 'exploded in spring… third-down favorite' - withdrawal override, triple-sourced) and Kaiuway (78.2/8 gm) give the pro-style install real TE material.
Behind them it's pedigree over production: former 4*s Small (186 as FR), Shelton ('6'4 spring hero'), James (ex-ND), plus Scott (S Alabama) - PS: 'less talented and exp'd… no true star yet.'
50 = average: one proven producer + TE quality + unproven youth.

Three-plus starters return: Taylor-Whitfield (66.7/895; third-year LT, 'most impressive spring lineman'), Bennett (60.4/564; year 7 via appeal), Van Hoy (13 gm), Hughes (injury return), Powers (65.4/376).
The transfer pair is quality: Buchanon (70.7/892; 2nd-team CUSA, 2 sacks over 1,600 snaps at FIU) + McKinney (66.5/390; near-4* transfer grade from OkSt) - 95 career FBS starts in the room.

PS: 'best OL in years… most size and strength of the Dykes era'; Athlon-Dykes: 'deepest of his tenure.' The counterweight: 49th-pctile run blocking and #103/#97 Run Push two straight years, with the interior arrangement unsettled (PS and Athlon print different centers).
52 = average-plus: pass-pro floor is real (78th pctile), the run-game proof isn't.

Seven of the top eight return from a 97th-pctile run defense (5th in B12): Oyewale (77.5/503 - best returning tape; withdrawal override, triple-sourced), Chapman (68.7/514; top-10 B12 pressures as a '24 FR), Din-Mbuh (68.7/488), Markis Deal (63.9/546; PS#26, 'poised for a breakout'), T.Johnson (68.1/307).
The only loss is Devean Deal (75.1/802; 13 st, 3.5 sk); adds are rotation-plus: Hayward (64.0/347 WKU) at STAR, Ofili (58.6/69 TTech), premium JUCOs Mickell (PS#6JC)/Cole.
P6 ('strength of the 2026 defense') and PS ('could be HC Dykes' best DL since he's been in Fort Worth') independently lead with this unit; the flaw is a 21st-pctile pass rush.
58 = solidly above average: elite run tape + returning mass, rush production unproven.

Both starters are gone and they were the unit: Elarms-Orr (84.4/897; 1st-team B12, 130 tackles - #4 in P4) and Obiazor (71.5/728; 88 tackles) - 'two of the top five fastest linebackers at the NFL Combine' (P6). The 93rd-pctile TACK grade walked out with them.

Carroll (71.5/219; 'set to emerge at MLB') is the one set piece with quality small-sample tape; WLB is Short (58.0/114 at VT) vs Teason (71.2/35) vs redshirt freshmen - 'more uncertainty' (PS), 'biggest question mark' (Athlon).
PS's 'won't drop too much' is opinion against two NFL-caliber departures. 42 = below average.

Johnson (72.7/906; 2nd-team All-B12, 96 tkl, 5 INT - 'a stud at SS' per PS) and Glover (71.0/659; 13 st) anchor the returning group; Gil Jackson (61.0/134; 6'3) is the spring-surge consensus at the other corner with Kylin Jackson (65.1/227) to nickel.
Losses are real: Clark (80.4/725; 3x All-B12), nickel Jordan (69.5/601), Canada (63.0/655) - from a unit that was already 43rd-pctile COV (#70 PDR).

Fields (72.8/775; C-USA Defensive POY, 92 tkl at LTech) fills Clark's spot; K.Carroll (74.6/722 CMU) and Parks (49.7/431 Colorado) add corner depth - 'outstanding depth, especially at corner… Stock Market rise in the PDR' (PS).
52 = average-plus: proven safety tape + depth, corner production still projection.
grades_detail.g5_guard_note: Fields' DPOY tape is CUSA-graded; unit grade leans on the returning P4 safeties, not the import

rationale_bullets: Both legs are verified: Lemmermann returns (PS's #2 kicker, 'NFL leg'; 15-22 with a 48-long in '24 before the '25 injury) alongside McCashland (9-12 in relief) - both kickers back.
Chance (LTech) brings elite punting volume: 66 punts, 47.3 avg, 43.3 net, 28 inside-20, long of 72; KR Everhart and PR Dwyer return.
'25 SPEC was 45th pctile (#91 STR) amid the kicker injury; PS explicitly projects a 'Stock Market climb.' 55 = above average on tape, short of elite until it shows at altitude.
